newsitem.title: GERMANY: No decision yet on budget freeze - German FinMin.
newsitem.headline: No decision yet on budget freeze - German FinMin.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel has not yet decided whether to impose a spending freeze to keep rising unemployment from undoing the 1997 budget, a ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
Waigel was waiting to see how the economy develops early in the year before requesting approval for any large expenditures, the spokesman told Reuters.
"There is no decision yet," he said. "We think the number of unemployed will drop considerably by the middle of the year at the latest."
Cut-backs in job and refugee programs, now under negotiation in parliament, would also reduce budgeted spending by some five billion marks, he said.
The mass circulation daily Bild daily had reported that Waigel would impose the spending restriction next week in the wake of January's surge in unemployment to a record 4.66 million.
